questions.prompt: What are the four parts of the pitch, in order?

options.text: Their problem, who we help, value, pricing
Who we help, their problem, one relevant value, a reason to continue
Who we help, the features, pricing, a reason to continue
One value, their problem, who we help, the ask

questions.prompt: Which two parts barely change from call to call?

options.text: Their problem and the relevant value
The relevant value and the reason to continue
Who we help and their problem
Who we help and the reason to continue

questions.reveal: Parts 2 and 3 change every time. That's where your pre-vetting and listening show up.

questions.prompt: How long should the pitch run?

options.text: Under twenty seconds
About a minute
Two to three minutes
As long as they stay engaged

questions.prompt: A rep's pitch: “Momence is an all-in-one platform with bookings, payments, marketing, an app and 24/7 support.” What's missing?

options.text: A clear line on who Momence actually helps
Pricing, so they can judge if it's worth it
Their problem, and one value that fits it
A longer list, so at least something lands

questions.reveal: That's reciting, not responding. Nothing in it is about the person on the phone.

questions.prompt: Which line is a strong part 4?

options.text: “Do you have time this week so we can show you how that would work for you?”
“Can I send you some information about everything we offer?”
“Would you like to hear a quick rundown of our pricing tiers?”
“Does that all make sense to you so far, or not really?”

questions.prompt: Pre-vetting gave you no specific hook for parts 2 and 3. What do you do?

options.text: Skip parts 2 and 3 and go straight to the ask
Run the full feature list until something lands
Ask them to walk you through their whole business
Use what's true of their industry or their software

questions.reveal: A relevant generalization beats a generic pitch.

questions.prompt: Which four themes does Momence's value sit under?

options.text: Price, features, support, integrations
Growth, retention, time and admin, client experience
Scheduling, payments, marketing, reporting
Speed, cost, ease of use, security

questions.prompt: She says, “People come once and we never see them again.” Which theme?

options.text: Retention
Growth
Time and admin
Client experience

questions.prompt: “I spend Sunday nights matching payments to bookings.” Which theme?

options.text: Growth
Retention
Client experience
Time and admin

questions.prompt: “Clients say booking is clunky, and we miss half their texts.” Which theme?

options.text: Retention
Time and admin
Client experience
Growth

questions.prompt: “I can't add classes because everything runs through me.” Which theme?

options.text: Retention
Growth
Client experience
Time and admin

questions.reveal: Growth is capped by whatever the owner can personally handle. That's a growth problem, not an admin one.

questions.prompt: A prospect has a retention problem. Which Momence tools answer it?

options.text: Two-way SMS, email and in-app messaging
Memberships, packs and point of sale
Automated sequences, on-demand content, community posts
Scheduling, staff management and reporting

questions.prompt: Pilates studio, two locations on MindBody. The front desk spends hours chasing class-pack renewals. Lead with…

options.text: “We have the best reporting dashboards in the industry.”
“Our app is the most downloaded in the wellness space.”
“We're cheaper than every other booking platform out there.”
“Automating the reminders and renewals your front desk chases by hand.”

questions.prompt: Wellness practice, 4 practitioners, scheduling and client messages in separate tools. Lead with…

options.text: “We replace your scheduling tool for a lot less money.”
“One place for scheduling and client messaging, instead of two.”
“We have a huge library of on-demand content for clients.”
“Most practices like yours switch over to us within a week.”

questions.prompt: Fitness studio: plenty of first visits, but clients stop showing after a few weeks. Lead with…

options.text: “Automated follow-up so new clients don't quietly disappear.”
“Payments and point of sale, all in one simple system.”
“A fully branded mobile app with your logo on it.”
“Staff scheduling with payroll exports built right in.”

questions.prompt: Drop-in dance studio on a basic booking tool, with class packs tracked in a spreadsheet. Lead with…

options.text: “Our loyalty program keeps dancers coming back every week.”
“We're the leading platform for every kind of studio there is.”
“Drop-ins, packs and memberships, all in one system.”
“Are you happy with the booking tool you're using right now?”

questions.prompt: Three true lead-with lines are written for a Pilates studio, a wellness practice and a fitness studio. Swap them between the three and every call fails. Why?

options.text: The product is different in each one
The value no longer matches what was noticed
The persona is wrong in every one
The statements are no longer true

questions.reveal: Same product, same true statements. Relevance is what breaks.

questions.prompt: Yoga studio with three locations. What's most worth leading with?

options.text: “We have the best pricing for multi-location studios.”
“Our app gets the highest ratings in the wellness space.”
“We can migrate all three of your sites over a weekend.”
“Running three schedules without three times the admin.”

questions.reveal: The other three are claims you can't back up on a cold call.

questions.prompt: You're talking to the founder. What usually lands?

options.text: Growth, and getting time back to run the business
Every detail of how staff scheduling works
How the front desk handles incoming messages
The technical specs of each integration

questions.prompt: The studio manager owns the schedule but not the software decision. Your pitch should…

options.text: Skip the pitch and just ask for the owner
Promise a price only the owner can approve
Speak to the schedule and admin they live in
Give the full owner-level growth pitch anyway

questions.prompt: Which titles can a meeting qualify with?

options.text: Owner, instructor, front desk, director
Owner, founder, director, studio or operations manager
Any staff member who agrees to the time
Only the owner or the founder

questions.prompt: Operations manager: “Our biggest headache is getting staff to cover classes.” Which value fits?

options.text: A branded mobile app for clients
Memberships and class packs
On-demand content and community posts
Staff management and scheduling in one place

questions.prompt: The front desk says they answer forty texts a day, but they don't touch the software decision. Best move?

options.text: Note the pain and ask who handles the software
Give them the full pitch so they pass it on
Book the meeting with them; they feel it most
Thank them and mark the lead Unqualified

questions.reveal: A meeting booked with front desk or instructors doesn't qualify. Their pain is your opener for the owner.

questions.prompt: How much does persona count toward qualification?

options.text: A formality once the business is a fit
Half the qualification
Something the AE checks after the demo
Only relevant for multi-location studios

questions.prompt: When does the pitch belong in a cold call?

options.text: Right after your opener, before any questions
At the very end, after you ask for the meeting
Once they've told you something isn't working
Only if they ask what Momence does

questions.prompt: She says, “No-shows are killing us.” Best pitch line?

options.text: “You said no-shows are the thing. That's usually where we help most. Worth showing you?”
“We have reminders, waitlists, payments, an app, marketing and two-way texting.”
“Most studios have no-shows. Honestly, it's just part of running a business.”
“What software are you using right now, and how long have you been on it?”

questions.prompt: You finish a strong fifteen-second pitch. Then what?

options.text: Keep going with a few more features
Go quiet and wait for them to fill it
Ask what their monthly budget is
Hand it back with a question or the ask

questions.prompt: She says she's happy with WellnessLiving. Your next line?

options.text: “WellnessLiving has a lot of gaps that we fix for studios.”
“Good to hear. If you could change one thing about it, what would it be?”
“Most of our clients came to us from WellnessLiving, actually.”
“No problem. I'll send some info in case that ever changes.”

questions.reveal: Don't knock what they chose. Ask what they'd change, then pitch to that.

questions.prompt: Which describes responding, not reciting?

options.text: The same words on every call
Mostly about Momence's features
Built from what they just said
Waiting for your turn to speak

questions.prompt: Which line is relevant, not just personalized?

options.text: “Saw you added a second Saturday class. Congrats on the growth!”
“Saw the second Saturday class. Is the rescheduling around it landing on you?”
“Love your studio's photos. The new space looks amazing.”
“Saw your five-star reviews. Your clients clearly love you.”
